definition: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is a subfield of artificial intelligence (AI) that uses generative models to generate text, images, videos, audio, software code or other forms of data.
details: These models learn the underlying patterns and structures of their training data, and use them to generate new data in response to input, which often takes the form of natural language prompts. The prevalence of generative AI tools has increased significantly since the AI boom in the 2020s. This boom was made possible by improvements in deep neural networks, particularly large language models (LLMs), which are based on the transformer architecture. Generative AI applications include chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, DeepSeek, Doubao, Google Gemini, Grok, Kimi and Qwen; text-to-image models such as DALL-E, Firefly, Stable Diffusion, and Midjourney; and text-to-video models such as Veo, LTX and Sora. Companies in a variety of sectors have used generative AI, including those in software development, healthcare, finance, entertainment, customer service, sales and marketing, art, writing, and product design. Generative AI has been used for cybercrime, and to deceive and manipulate people through fake news and deepfakes. Generative AI models have been trained on copyrighted works without the rightholders' permission. Many generative AI systems are reliant on large-scale data centers, whose environmental impacts include electronic waste, consumption of fresh water for cooling, and high energy consumption that is estimated to be growing steadily.

explainer.lead: Generative AI creates new text, images, video, audio, code, and other data from patterns learned during training. It powers widely used chatbots and media-generation tools, while also raising concerns about deception, copyright, and the environmental cost of large data centers.

tiers.eli5: Generative AI is a bit like learning to draw by studying lots of pictures, then making a new picture when someone asks. You might type a request, such as “draw a cat wearing a space helmet,” and the computer creates a new image. It can also write stories, make sounds or videos, and produce computer code.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use generative AI through chatbots such as ChatGPT and Gemini, text-to-image systems such as Stable Diffusion, and text-to-video systems such as Sora, often with natural-language prompts. Applications span software development, customer service, marketing, healthcare, finance, and design. Practical concerns include potential misuse for fake news and deepfakes, training on copyrighted works without permission, and the energy, water, and electronic-waste impacts of supporting data centers.
tiers.paperLevel: Given training data D and an input x, often a natural-language prompt, a generative model learns patterns and structure from D and generates new data y, where y may be text, an image, video, audio, code, or another data form. Its growth in the 2020s was enabled by improved deep neural networks, especially transformer-based large language models. Known problems include use in cybercrime and manipulation, unauthorized training on copyrighted works, and substantial data-center resource demands.

explainer.example: A user asks a chatbot, “Write a short reminder that my dentist appointment is at 9 a.m. Tuesday.” The model uses patterns learned from text to generate a new reminder matching that request, rather than requiring a person to write it first.

explainer.intuition: Instead of following a fixed template for every answer, a generative model learns regularities in many examples and uses them to produce something new. A prompt guides what kind of output it generates.
howItWorks: Collect training data containing examples of the desired kind of data.
Train a generative model to learn the data’s underlying patterns and structures.
Provide an input, often a natural-language prompt.
Use the learned patterns to generate a new response, such as text, an image, or code.
explainer.whyItMatters: Generative AI has spread across software development, healthcare, finance, entertainment, customer service, marketing, art, writing, and product design. The same capabilities can also support cybercrime, fake news, and deepfakes, making its benefits and risks important to consider together.
misconceptions: Generative AI is not all of AI; it is a subfield focused on generating new data.
Its output is not limited to text: it can also include images, video, audio, code, and other data.
A prompt is often natural language, but the generated result is new data rather than simply a spoken or written description of the prompt.
